roleTypes.label: Enabling condition
roleTypes.definition: A circumstance that makes a route possible; it does not by itself establish a hazard.

roleTypes.label: Unsafe control action
roleTypes.definition: An action or omission linked to its controller, hazardous context and affected constraint.

roleTypes.label: Loss scenario
roleTypes.definition: An explanation of how control can become inadequate, including feedback and execution problems.

roleTypes.label: Hazardous state
roleTypes.definition: A system state that can produce a loss together with relevant environmental conditions.

roleTypes.label: Optional amplifier
roleTypes.definition: A factor that could strengthen a route but is not required in every version.

roleTypes.label: Loss
roleTypes.definition: An outcome stakeholders seek to prevent, kept distinct from its contributing causes.

roleTypes.label: Recovery
roleTypes.definition: A response re-establishes enforceable safety constraints within a specified boundary; success requires verification.

limitingConditions.example: Independently enforced review, access bounds or effective interruption.
limitingConditions.question: Which specified mechanism blocks the transition, and what demonstrates that it works?

limitingConditions.example: The system cannot perform the required research, deception or physical task.
limitingConditions.question: Would increased capability remove this limit?

limitingConditions.example: The necessary access, resources or institutional delegation is unavailable.
limitingConditions.question: Can the system or another actor acquire what is missing?

limitingConditions.example: Activity ends for a reason that does not establish an effective safeguard.
limitingConditions.question: What actually ended the episode, and would that circumstance recur?

title: Misleading threat assessment and nuclear escalation
summary: Could a convincing but false threat picture move a nuclear decision beyond effective correction?
scope: A hypothetical crisis-warning, intelligence-assessment and nuclear-command system in which AI shapes advice to human decision-makers. Sensor input, independent scrutiny, authorization and correction are modeled separately.
purpose: Prevent nuclear harm caused by materially false threat assessment while preserving verified information, accountable decisions and effective correction.
boundary: No real country’s classified command arrangements are claimed. Human authorization remains explicit. The two NORAD records are historical non-AI analogies for information and control mechanisms; they are not evidence of AI nuclear use.
numbering: 01–06 identify scenario milestones, not STPA steps or measured proximity to nuclear war. R is an intervention before irreversible nuclear use. Historical overlays at 02 establish neither the preceding AI reliance nor the later decision.
bowtie: The centre, H1 at 04, is nuclear force committed on a materially false premise without effective correction. Misleading information and inadequate scrutiny are left-side threats; actual detonation and wider exchange remain conditional consequences.
schema: A first-pass STPA reconstruction with human decision authority, machine information, verification, control execution and recovery kept distinct. The bow-tie summarizes selected loss scenarios.
limits: This analysis is provisional and requires national-doctrine, warning-system and crisis-decision expertise. Four unsafe-action categories are illustrated, not exhaustively assessed. The historical records show warning failures and corrective changes; they do not establish AI reliance, a launch order, a measured escalation probability or the performance of modern nuclear safeguards.

losses.title: Nuclear detonation and mass casualties
losses.text: People suffer death, injury and long-term harm from nuclear use initiated on a false assessment.

losses.title: Wider war and cascading deprivation
losses.text: Further exchange and disruption damage populations and essential systems across regions. A famine continuation additionally depends on physical and food-system conditions.

hazards.title: Nuclear force committed without effective correction
hazards.text: A materially false threat assessment leads to consequential nuclear commitment while the command system cannot reliably correct or stop the decision before irreversible use.

hazards.title: An unverified threat picture governs the decision
hazards.text: Decision-makers receive an apparently authoritative assessment that obscures material uncertainty or contradictory evidence during a crisis.

hazards.title: Correction loses the intervention window
hazards.text: A valid correction or cancellation cannot be delivered, interpreted and executed before the relevant action becomes irreversible.

controllers.title: National decision authority
controllers.responsibility: Decide whether to authorize, defer or cancel nuclear use under the applicable doctrine, accounting for contrary evidence.
controllers.feedback: Independent assessment, uncertainty, alternative explanations and action status.
controllers.assumption: The existence of a human decision-maker is not evidence of meaningful scrutiny.

controllers.title: Intelligence and warning assessment team
controllers.responsibility: Corroborate warnings, challenge AI conclusions and communicate material uncertainty to C1.
controllers.feedback: Independent sensor and intelligence channels, provenance and disconfirming observations.
controllers.assumption: Multiple reports may share one erroneous upstream source.

controllers.title: AI decision-support system
controllers.responsibility: Organize information within its approved scope and expose uncertainty and source provenance.
controllers.feedback: Authenticated observations, analyst corrections and use restrictions.
controllers.assumption: Fluent explanations and confident rankings can be wrong without any deceptive objective.

controllers.title: Warning-system operations and assurance
controllers.responsibility: Maintain operational input integrity, separate tests from live warning and flag invalid or inconsistent messages.
controllers.feedback: Sensor status, message checks, test provenance and independent monitoring.
controllers.assumption: Correct transmission does not establish that the underlying assessment is true.

controllers.title: Human authorization and execution chain
controllers.responsibility: Execute only valid authorized actions and apply valid cancellation while that remains possible.
controllers.feedback: Order status, conflicting or canceled authority and confirmed execution state.
controllers.assumption: Recovery may be impossible after an irreversible physical commitment.

controllers.title: Independent crisis communication function
controllers.responsibility: Bring credible external clarification and de-escalation information into the assessment and decision process.
controllers.feedback: Authenticated communications, acknowledgments and unresolved contradictions.
controllers.assumption: An available channel may fail to deliver useful clarification in time.

controllers.title: Weapon execution system
controllers.responsibility: Operate only within valid authorization and accept an effective hold or cancellation while action remains reversible.
controllers.feedback: Validated command state, independent status checks and execution-state reporting.
controllers.assumption: This abstract role supplies no description of a real weapon system or its command mechanisms.

controlLoops.action: Admit operational data or withhold invalid input
controlLoops.feedback: Provenance checks, source status and downstream data use.

controlLoops.action: Submit a threat assessment or require further corroboration
controlLoops.feedback: Decision-maker questions and independent disconfirming evidence.

controlLoops.action: Authorize, defer or cancel nuclear use
controlLoops.feedback: Independent findings and the remaining intervention window.

controlLoops.action: Release execution or apply a valid cancellation
controlLoops.feedback: Independently confirmed action status and receipt at each relevant element.
Receipt, assessment changes and outstanding ambiguity.

constraints.title: Separate tests from operational warning
constraints.text: Test, simulated and invalid data must remain distinguishable from operational warning throughout processing and presentation.
constraints.test: Can a bounded exercise inject test or invalid data without it ever appearing as an authenticated operational warning?
constraints.limit: Separation of test data does not address a false but internally consistent real-world assessment.

constraints.title: Corroborate through independent evidence
constraints.text: Material threat conclusions must retain provenance and be checked against genuinely independent information, with contradictions visible to decision-makers.
constraints.test: Does contradictory evidence from an independent channel change the assessment, rather than being summarized away?
constraints.limit: Shared upstream errors, missing observations or common dependence on one AI summary.

constraints.title: Protect deliberation and dissent
constraints.text: Authorization must not treat an AI recommendation as sufficient proof; available uncertainty and credible alternatives must reach accountable decision-makers in time.
constraints.test: In a safe crisis exercise, do decision-makers defer or revise a decision when independent evidence invalidates its premise?
constraints.limit: Time pressure, doctrine, prior beliefs and institutional pressure can overwhelm nominal human review.

constraints.title: Verify correction before irreversible action
constraints.text: The command system must preserve and verify a valid correction or cancellation until the relevant action is irreversible.
constraints.test: In a simulation, is a valid cancellation received and confirmed effective before the modeled point of irreversibility?
constraints.limit: A cancellation sent too late cannot undo a detonation; the real intervention window is doctrine and system dependent.

constraints.title: Reassess after changing the system
constraints.text: Changes to warning software, message formats and decision support must be independently checked for new common failures before operational reliance.
constraints.test: Do representative abnormal-input and communication exercises still reveal faults after a system or AI update?
constraints.limit: Fixing a known fault is not proof that novel misleading information will be recognized.

nodes.title: A crisis decision relies on AI-organized intelligence
nodes.text: AI-generated organization or recommendations materially influence crisis assessment.
nodes.requires: Consequential reliance in a crisis, not simply the presence of AI software.
nodes.mechanism: AI can shape salience, framing and confidence in information that informs a human decision.

nodes.title: A false picture resembles an imminent attack
nodes.text: Error, misleading presentation or invalid input produces an exaggerated apparent threat.
nodes.requires: The false information reaches the assessment process and matters to its conclusions.
nodes.mechanism: Data contamination, unreliable inference or presentation can make an incorrect warning appear credible.

nodes.title: Independent scrutiny does not correct the premise
nodes.text: Contradictory evidence and material uncertainty do not change the recommendation in time.
nodes.requires: Available scrutiny is ineffective or missing during the relevant decision window.
nodes.mechanism: Time pressure or an inadequate process model can turn a tentative warning into an unjustified conclusion.

nodes.title: Nuclear use is committed on a false premise
nodes.text: Human authorization commits nuclear force while effective correction is absent.
nodes.requires: A materially false premise, consequential authorization and ineffective cancellation before irreversible use.
nodes.mechanism: An informational error becomes a hazardous system state when the authorized control chain commits force without effective correction.

nodes.title: A nuclear detonation causes mass harm
nodes.text: The execution chain carries out the decision and a weapon detonates.
nodes.requires: Successful execution, delivery and detonation, with no effective interruption.
nodes.mechanism: Authorization is not detonation; the physical execution route must also complete.

nodes.title: Further exchange widens the consequences
nodes.text: Additional nuclear use and cascading disruption harm populations beyond the first strike.
nodes.requires: Retaliation or further exchange; famine additionally requires sufficient atmospheric effects and failed food-system adaptation.
nodes.mechanism: Neither one detonation nor a false warning establishes the scale or continuation of a wider catastrophe.

nodes.title: The decision is corrected and action stops
nodes.text: Independent information changes the decision and cancellation is verified before irreversible action.
nodes.requires: Credible contrary information, authority to revise the decision and a reachable execution chain.
nodes.mechanism: Recovery requires an effective change in action; detection or a transmitted cancellation alone is insufficient.

unsafeActions.context: A warning is materially uncertain and independent observations could change the recommendation before authorization.

unsafeActions.action: Reports a threat as established despite unresolved contradictions
unsafeActions.context: The report will be used for a consequential decision and hides evidence against the premise.

unsafeActions.action: Authorizes nuclear use on an inadequately verified assessment
unsafeActions.context: Material false information governs the decision and the remaining control path cannot ensure correction.

unsafeActions.action: Issues cancellation after the intervention window
unsafeActions.context: The revised information arrives while cancellation is still possible but the correction is delayed until irreversible action.

unsafeActions.action: Ends a hold while the premise remains unresolved
unsafeActions.context: Releasing the hold restores an active authorization based on the unresolved false assessment.

scenarios.title: Invalid machine information enters operational warning
scenarios.text: Test information or a processing fault reaches operational warning. AI reliance is an additional hypothetical condition, not a feature of the historical comparison.
scenarios.unknown: Whether modern input controls would prevent comparable contamination and how any AI assessment would use it.

scenarios.title: A convincing synthesis suppresses contradictory evidence
scenarios.text: Analysts treat apparent agreement or a fluent summary as independent confirmation while several reports share one source or omit contrary observations.
scenarios.unknown: Actual source independence and whether contradictions reach the decision-maker.

scenarios.title: Time pressure converts uncertainty into authorization
scenarios.text: A permissive posture, pressure to act or an inadequate model of the warning leads to consequential authorization without resolving material uncertainty.
scenarios.unknown: The applicable doctrine, decision window and influence of AI advice in the specific system.

scenarios.title: Correction cannot stop physical execution
scenarios.text: A valid correction is delayed, not received, misinterpreted or ineffective; alternatively, a hold ends while false-premise authorization remains active.
scenarios.unknown: Where action becomes irreversible and which cancellation effects can be independently confirmed.

scenarios.title: Initial harm develops into a wider catastrophe
scenarios.text: Further exchange can expand direct and systemic harm. A famine route requires sufficiently large physical disruption plus inadequate food reserves, adaptation and distribution; neither follows automatically from one strike.
scenarios.unknown: Scale of further exchange and resilience of affected physical and social systems.

sources.title: Leveson & Thomas · STPA Handbook (2018)

sources.use: AI decision-support risks and cross-checking proposals; not a documented autonomous launch.

sources.access: Full report retrieved; printed pages 3 and 13–14 inspected
sources.hashScope: Tool-returned text extracts from the source; not a full-text content hash

sources.use: Conditional climatic and food-system continuation; not an estimate for this pathway.

targets.label: Erroneous machine information can resemble an attack warning

assessments.scope: Warning-input analogy only. AI dependence, failed independent scrutiny, a launch order and nuclear harm are not established. The barrier shown is a documented post-incident corrective design, not proof of what prevented nuclear use during the episode.

trace.text: Simulated data reached the operational warning system.
The system indicated a mass raid.
A later off-site facility separated software testing from operational warning.

barriers.title: Separate test and operational systems
barriers.action: NORAD installed an off-site facility for software development and testing after simulated data reached operational warning.
barriers.efficacy: The report documents stronger separation of test and operational systems; it does not report a controlled measure of reliability.
barriers.durability: Post-incident strengthening is documented. How reliably it would handle a novel failure or modern AI output remains untested here.
barriers.failure: A misleading real-world input or assessment can remain possible even when tests are physically separate.

view.failureRoute: A different source of misleading information

dependencies.label: Scope of the known failure

reinforcement.proposal: Test the revised control against safe, representative fault and provenance scenarios.
reinforcement.test: Verify that incorrect inputs are identified before they can drive a consequential assessment.

reach.local: Simulated data entered the operational warning system and produced false attack indications. A separate development facility was subsequently established.
reach.systemic: Warning-input analogy only. AI dependence, failed independent scrutiny, a launch order and nuclear harm are not established.

assessments.scope: A second warning-system mechanism. No claim is made that machine output determined a leader’s nuclear decision. The barrier shown is a documented post-incident corrective design, not proof of what prevented nuclear use during the episode.

Transmission and message-check procedures were changed.

barriers.title: Transmission and message checks
barriers.action: NORAD changed transmission procedures and message checks after a processor fault generated false warning information.
barriers.efficacy: The report documents corrective changes to the warning path; it does not measure their performance against novel faults.
barriers.durability: Post-incident strengthening is documented. How reliably it would handle a novel failure or modern AI output remains untested here.
barriers.failure: Accurate transmission can still carry an incorrect underlying assessment.

NOR-1979.title: NORAD 1979 false warning
NOR-1979.observed: A historical non-AI warning failure was followed by a documented corrective change.
NOR-1979.notEstablished: Neither AI reliance, a launch order nor the effectiveness of the corrective design against modern AI is established.
NOR-1979.limit: A historical non-AI warning failure was followed by a documented corrective change. Neither AI reliance, a launch order nor the effectiveness of the corrective design against modern AI is established.

separate-test-system.title: Separate test and operational systems
separate-test-system.result: Strengthened after the incident; efficacy unmeasured.
separate-test-system.conditionBasis: A documented post-incident design change added protection against the identified failure; this is structural reinforcement, not measured universal effectiveness.
separate-test-system.strongerAI: Separation still depends on preserving the operational data boundary; more capable AI can produce misleading assessments from valid live inputs that this test-data barrier does not address.

reinforcement.proposal: Exercise independent warning and assessment checks against representative new failure modes.
reinforcement.test: Does disconfirming evidence stop an incorrect assessment before consequential action?

NOR-1980.title: NORAD 1980 false warning
NOR-1980.observed: A historical non-AI warning failure was followed by a documented corrective change.
NOR-1980.notEstablished: Neither AI reliance, a launch order nor the effectiveness of the corrective design against modern AI is established.
NOR-1980.limit: A historical non-AI warning failure was followed by a documented corrective change. Neither AI reliance, a launch order nor the effectiveness of the corrective design against modern AI is established.

message-checks.title: Transmission and message checks
message-checks.result: Strengthened after the incident; efficacy unmeasured.
message-checks.conditionBasis: A documented post-incident design change added protection against the identified failure; this is structural reinforcement, not measured universal effectiveness.
message-checks.strongerAI: Message checks depend on detecting corruption in transmission; a more capable AI can deliver a confidently wrong assessment through an intact message path.

reinforcement.proposal: Exercise independent warning and assessment checks against representative new failure modes.
reinforcement.test: Does disconfirming evidence stop an incorrect assessment before consequential action?

presentation.fidelity: The two records are historical comparisons at 02. Reinforced means a documented corrective design after the incident; it does not identify the historical stopping mechanism or prove future efficacy.
presentation.barrierQuestion: Will this control still work when misleading information becomes more persuasive, or does it only address a known fault?
